key_insight: The study shows that biomedical AI explanations can be made machine-verifiable by linking each claim to explicit radiomic evidence, separate from prediction quality.
clinical_relevance: This could improve trust and auditability of AI-assisted brain tumor imaging reports by making statements traceable to patient-specific data.
method: Aligned UPenn-GBM radiomics with de novo CaPTk features from standardized MRI and expert segmentations.
Built a neuro-semantic evidence ledger across 1,728 MRI features from T1, T1GD, T2, and FLAIR across three tumor regions.
Tested deterministic claim verification, controlled degradation, and an LLM-based claim extraction pilot.
evidence_signal: Across the benchmark, semantic-state agreement was moderate overall (median 0.786, weighted kappa 0.709), the verifier reached 100% exact-set accuracy on 6,620 corrupted claims, and verification stayed 1.000 even as prediction AUC dropped from 0.899 to 0.500.
watch_item: The framework verifies whether claims match available evidence, but it does not guarantee strong clinical prediction performance or broadly generalizable external accuracy.
paper_title: Evidence-Bound Reasoning: Neuro-Semantic Verification of Biomedical AI in Glioblastoma Radiogenomics
